![](Images/banner_health_analytics.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"} # Health Analytics with R ## A Comprehensive Tutorial Series

🏥 Health Analytics with R

From Raw EHR Data to Production-Ready Clinical Models

Modules 8 modules · 62 notebooks · ~450 code cells
Level Intermediate to Advanced · Healthcare data science background assumed
Language R 4.3+ · Quarto-compatible
Dataset Synthetic (MIMIC-III inspired) · seed = 42 throughout
Author Dr. Zia U. Ahmed · Upatta Analytics · zia207 @ GitHub
*** ## 1. Why Health Analytics with R? Healthcare generates more data per person than almost any other industry — electronic health records, claims databases, imaging, genomics, wearables, and administrative files — yet much of it remains under-analysed. R has become the language of choice for many epidemiologists and health data scientists because of its rich ecosystem spanning statistics, machine learning, natural language processing, geospatial analysis, and production deployment. **This series bridges three gaps that most textbooks leave open:** 1. **Clinically meaningful examples** — every dataset, model, and metric is grounded in real healthcare problems: readmission prediction, drug optimisation, spatial health inequities, causal effects of treatment. 2. **End-to-end thinking** — notebooks do not stop at model accuracy. They continue through calibration, fairness, explainability, API serving, monitoring, and clinical governance. 3. **Reproducibility by design** — code is written as it would be in a health system data science team: version-pinned environments, SHA-256 data manifests, logged pipelines, and CI/CD-ready test suites. > **Who is this for?** Health informatics professionals, clinical data scientists, epidemiologists, public health researchers, and graduate students who know R basics and want to apply it rigorously to healthcare problems. ## 2. Series Architecture The eight modules form two learning tracks that can be taken independently or sequentially. ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TRACK A: PHARMACY & CLINICAL ANALYTICS │ │ │ │ MOD-01 MOD-02 MOD-03 MOD-04 MOD-05 │ │ R Exploratory Statistical Machine NLP for │ │ Foundations → Data Analysis → Inference → Learning → Clinical Text │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TRACK B: POPULATION HEALTH & DEPLOYMENT │ │ │ │ MOD-06 MOD-07 MOD-08 │ │ Causal → Spatial → Reproducible │ │ Inference Epidemiology Research & │ │ Deployment │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ All modules share: seed=42 · MIMIC-III-inspired synthetic data · 300 dpi figures ``` Each module contains **8 notebooks** following a consistent arc: `Concepts → Core method → Case study → Extension → Capstone` ## 3. ── Quick-start: a taste of what each module delivers ────────────────────────── set.seed(42) N <- 1800 sigmoid <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x)) # ── Shared synthetic cohort ────────────────────────────────────────────────── age <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 63, 14), 18), 90)) los <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 28)) hf <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.22) dm <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.35) copd <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.18) payer <- sample( c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.10) ) logit <- -3.2 + 0.6 * hf + 0.5 * dm + 0.3 * copd + 0.02 * (age - 63) + 0.2 * (los > 7) readmit <- rbinom(N, 1, sigmoid(logit)) cvd_rate <- 180 + 1.4 * rnorm(N, 10, 5) + 12 * rnorm(N, 0, 1) df <- tibble( age = age, los = los, hf = hf, dm = dm, copd = copd, payer = payer, readmit = readmit, cvd_rate = cvd_rate ) cat(sprintf("Cohort: N=%s | Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n", format(N, big.mark = ","), mean(readmit) * 100)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cohort: N=1,800 | Readmission rate: 6.1% ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("Building preview figure ...\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Building preview figure ... ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── 8-panel preview figure — one panel per module ─────────────────────────── BLUE <- "#2563EB"; RED <- "#DC2626"; GREEN <- "#16A34A" GOLD <- "#D97706"; PURPLE <- "#7C3AED"; TEAL <- "#0D9488" GRAY <- "#6B7280"; PINK <- "#DB2777" theme_preview <- function(base_size = 9) { theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) + theme( plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA), legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, lineheight = 1.1) ) } # Stratified 80/20 split (matches tidymodels/rsample strata, seed = 42) set.seed(42) df <- df %>% mutate(.row = dplyr::row_number()) train <- df %>% group_by(readmit) %>% slice_sample(prop = 0.8) %>% ungroup() test <- dplyr::anti_join(df, train, by = ".row") n_tr <- nrow(train) n1 <- sum(train$readmit == 1) n0 <- n_tr - n1 train$w <- ifelse(train$readmit == 1, n_tr / (2 * n1), n_tr / (2 * n0)) model <- glm( readmit ~ age + los + hf + dm + copd, family = quasibinomial(), data = train, weights = w ) prob <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = test, type = "response")) y_te <- test$readmit roc_curve_df <- function(y, p) { y <- as.integer(y) o <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE) y <- y[o] tp <- cumsum(y) fp <- cumsum(1L - y) tibble( fpr = c(0, fp / max(fp[length(fp)], 1), 1), tpr = c(0, tp / max(tp[length(tp)], 1), 1) ) } auc_trap <- function(fpr, tpr) { o <- order(fpr) fpr <- fpr[o] tpr <- tpr[o] sum(diff(fpr) * (utils::head(tpr, -1) + utils::tail(tpr, -1)) / 2) } roc_df <- roc_curve_df(y_te, prob) auc <- auc_trap(roc_df$fpr, roc_df$tpr) # ── Panel 1: MOD-02 · EDA — readmission by payer ───────────────────────────── overall_rate <- mean(df$readmit) * 100 payer_r <- df %>% group_by(payer) %>% summarise(rate = mean(readmit) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(desc(rate)) %>% mutate( payer = factor(payer, levels = payer), fill = ifelse(rate > overall_rate + 2, RED, BLUE) ) p1 <- ggplot(payer_r, aes(payer, rate, fill = fill)) + geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) + geom_hline(yintercept = overall_rate, colour = GRAY, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", rate)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6) + scale_fill_identity() + labs( y = "30-day readmission rate (%)", x = NULL, title = "MOD-02 · EDA\nReadmission Rate by Payer" ) + theme_preview() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 18, hjust = 1, size = 8)) # ── Panel 2: MOD-03 · Statistics — survival curve ───────────────────────────── t_max <- 30 times <- seq(0, t_max, length.out = 200) surv_df <- bind_rows( tibble( days = times, surv = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 1], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)), group = "Heart Failure" ), tibble( days = times, surv = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 0], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)), group = "No HF" ) ) p2 <- ggplot(surv_df, aes(days, surv, colour = group, fill = group)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = surv), alpha = 0.08, colour = NA) + geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) + labs( x = "Days", y = "Survival (in-hospital)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "MOD-03 · Statistics\nKaplan-Meier by HF Status" ) + theme_preview() + theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.88), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5)) # ── Panel 3: MOD-04 · ML — ROC curve ───────────────────────────────────────── p3 <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), fill = RED, alpha = 0.10) + geom_line(colour = RED, linewidth = 1.1) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) + annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = 0.18, label = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc), colour = RED, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") + labs( x = "1 − Specificity", y = "Sensitivity", title = "MOD-04 · Machine Learning\nROC Curve — Readmission Model" ) + theme_preview() # ── Panel 4: MOD-05 · NLP — entity frequency bar ───────────────────────────── entities <- c("MEDICATION", "DIAGNOSIS", "PROCEDURE", "LAB_VALUE", "VITAL_SIGN", "DATE", "PROVIDER") counts <- c(340, 285, 198, 423, 312, 510, 87) + sample(-15:15, 7, replace = TRUE) ner_df <- tibble( entity = factor(entities, levels = rev(entities)), count = counts, fill = c(BLUE, RED, GREEN, GOLD, PURPLE, TEAL, PINK) ) p4 <- ggplot(ner_df, aes(count, entity, fill = fill)) + geom_col(colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) + geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.6) + scale_fill_identity() + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(ner_df$count) * 1.12)) + labs( x = "Entity count (synthetic discharge notes)", y = NULL, title = "MOD-05 · Clinical NLP\nclinicalBERT Named Entity Recognition" ) + theme_preview() # ── Panel 5: MOD-06 · Causal — Love plot (balance) ─────────────────────────── love_df <- tibble( covariate = factor(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"), levels = rev(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"))), Unadjusted = c(0.38, 0.27, 0.45, 0.31, 0.22), `IPTW weighted` = c(0.04, 0.03, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02) ) %>% pivot_longer(-covariate, names_to = "method", values_to = "smd") p5 <- ggplot(love_df, aes(smd, covariate, fill = method)) + geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.32, colour = "white", alpha = 0.80) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Unadjusted" = RED, "IPTW weighted" = BLUE)) + labs( x = "Absolute SMD", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "MOD-06 · Causal Inference\nLove Plot — IPTW Balance" ) + theme_preview() + theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.22), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5)) # ── Panel 6: MOD-07 · Geospatial — synthetic scatter map ───────────────────── set.seed(7) N_c <- 200 geo <- tibble( lon = runif(N_c, -120, -70), lat = runif(N_c, 28, 48) ) %>% mutate(cvd = 180 + 1.4 * (lon + 95) + 12 * rnorm(N_c, 0, 1)) tt <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 120) circ <- tibble(x = -100 + 8 * cos(tt), y = 33 + 8 * sin(tt)) p6 <- ggplot(geo, aes(lon, lat, colour = cvd)) + geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.80) + geom_path(data = circ, aes(x, y), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) + annotate("text", x = -100, y = 24.5, label = "Hot spot\n(scan stat)", size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") + scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#1A9850", "#FDE725", "#D73027"), name = "CVD rate/100k") + labs( x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", title = "MOD-07 · Spatial Epi\nCVD Mortality + Cluster Detection" ) + theme_preview() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 7), legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5)) # ── Panel 7: MOD-08 · Deployment — drift monitoring ────────────────────────── quarters <- c("23-Q1", "23-Q2", "23-Q3", "23-Q4", "24-Q1", "24-Q2") drift <- tibble( quarter = factor(quarters, levels = quarters), Overall = c(0.789, 0.784, 0.780, 0.771, 0.758, 0.745), `Black/AA` = c(0.775, 0.769, 0.764, 0.751, 0.735, 0.718) ) %>% pivot_longer(-quarter, names_to = "group", values_to = "auc") p7 <- ggplot(drift, aes(quarter, auc, colour = group, group = group)) + annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0.789 - 0.05, ymax = 0.789 - 0.03, fill = "orange", alpha = 0.10) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.789 - 0.03, colour = "orange", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.6) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.789 - 0.05, colour = RED, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.6) + geom_line(aes(linetype = group), linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Overall" = BLUE, "Black/AA" = RED)) + scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Overall" = "solid", "Black/AA" = "dashed")) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.68, 0.82)) + labs( x = NULL, y = "AUC-ROC", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL, title = "MOD-08 · Deployment\nModel Drift & Fairness Monitoring" ) + theme_preview() + theme(legend.position = c(0.28, 0.22), legend.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8)) # ── Panel 8: Series overview donut ─────────────────────────────────────────── donut <- tibble( label = c("Foundations\n& EDA", "Statistics\n& Survival", "Machine\nLearning", "Clinical NLP", "Causal\nInference", "Spatial Epi", "Deployment\n& MLOps"), n = 8, fill = c(TEAL, BLUE, RED, GREEN, GOLD, PURPLE, GRAY) ) %>% mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label)) p8 <- ggplot(donut, aes(x = 2, y = n, fill = fill)) + geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 1) + geom_text(aes(x = 2.75, label = label), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.4, lineheight = 0.9) + annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0, label = "62", size = 8, fontface = "bold", colour = "#1F2937") + annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0, label = "\n\nnotebooks", size = 3.1, colour = GRAY) + coord_polar(theta = "y", start = pi / 2) + xlim(0.5, 3.3) + scale_fill_identity() + labs(title = "HealthR Series\nModule Distribution") + theme_void() + theme( plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.1) ) preview <- (p1 | p2 | p3 | p4) / (p5 | p6 | p7 | p8) + plot_annotation( title = "Health Analytics with R · Series Preview", theme = theme( plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5), plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA) ) ) preview_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod00") dir.create(preview_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) preview_path <- file.path(preview_dir, "healthr_intro_preview.png") ggsave(preview_path, preview, width = 22, height = 14, dpi = 180, bg = "white") print(preview) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](MOD00_NTRO_HealthR_Tutorial_Series_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=2112} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("Preview figure rendered.\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Preview figure rendered. ``` ::: ::: ## 4. How to Use This Series ### Option A — RStudio / Posit Cloud (Recommended for beginners) Open any `.qmd` file in RStudio or [Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/). Quarto renders HTML with a table of contents; Posit Cloud provides a free hosted R session. ```r # Run this once per machine to install any missing packages source("packages.R") ``` ### Option B — Local Quarto / RStudio ```bash # 1. Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/zia207/Health-Analytics-with-Python.git cd Health-Analytics-with-Python/Health-Analytics-R # 2. Install all dependencies Rscript packages.R # 3. Open the project in RStudio, or render from the command line quarto preview ``` ### Option C — VS Code + Quarto Extension Open any `.qmd` file directly in VS Code with the Quarto extension. Select the R kernel created above. *** ### Running Order ``` New to health data science? → MOD-01 → MOD-02 → MOD-03 → MOD-04 Want ML for clinical prediction? → MOD-04 (then MOD-05 for NLP, MOD-08 for deployment) Interested in causal inference? → MOD-06 (requires MOD-03 background) Spatial epidemiology focus? → MOD-07 (requires MOD-02 EDA) Building a production pipeline? → MOD-08 (works standalone) ``` ## 5. Series Conventions **Reproducibility first** - All notebooks use `set.seed(42)` as the first executable cell - Synthetic datasets are generated in-memory; no downloads required - A shared helper pattern regenerates the same cohort across all notebooks in a module **Code style** - tidyverse style, `snake_case`, max line length 100 characters - Documented function signatures with argument descriptions - Comments on every function: purpose, args, returns - Tested with `testthat`; CI via GitHub Actions **Figures** - All publication figures saved at **300 dpi** via `ggsave(..., dpi = 300)` - Consistent colour palette: `#2563EB` (blue) / `#DC2626` (red) / `#16A34A` (green) - Colourblind-accessible palettes used throughout **Dataset conventions** | Symbol | Meaning | |--------|---------| | `N` | sample size | | `df` | primary working data frame / tibble | | `X_tr, X_te` | train / test feature matrices | | `y_tr, y_te` | train / test target vectors | | `FEATURES` | list of predictor column names | | `TRUE_EFFECT` | known simulation parameter (for validation) | **Notebook structure (every NB follows this pattern)** 1. Title, learning objectives, estimated time 2. `## 1. Setup` — imports, dataset generation, seed 3. `## 2–N` — core content sections 4. Knowledge Check — 5 questions 5. Exercises — at least one executable cell per exercise 6. `--- Next → NB-0X` — explicit navigation footer ## 6. Datasets & Data Ethics ### Synthetic data — why not real patient data? All notebooks use **synthetic data** generated with controlled random seeds. This approach: - Allows open publication without IRB restrictions or HIPAA concerns - Lets us embed **known ground-truth effects** so learners can verify their results - Reproduces identical results across operating systems and time The synthetic data are designed to mimic the statistical properties of real EHR data (MIMIC-III), with realistic covariate distributions, correlation structures, and outcome rates. ### Data Ethics Principles Embedded in This Series | Module | Embedded ethics topic | |--------|----------------------| | MOD-04 | Calibration and algorithmic fairness across demographic groups | | MOD-05 | De-identification of PHI before NLP model training | | MOD-06 | Causal assumptions and the limits of observational data | | MOD-07 | Environmental justice and spatial health disparities | | MOD-08 | Model Cards, governance checklists, patient-facing explanations | > **A note on race in clinical models:** Where race/ethnicity appears in the synthetic data, it is used to *audit fairness* — never as a predictor variable. The series explicitly demonstrates how models can encode proxy-bias even when race is excluded from features. ## Technology Stack ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Full technology stack visualisation ─────────────────────────────────────── layers <- tibble( xmin = 0.3, xmax = 15.7, ymin = c(0.3, 1.5, 2.8, 4.1, 5.4), ymax = c(0.3, 1.5, 2.8, 4.1, 5.4) + 1.1, face = c("#F8FAFC", "#FDF4FF", "#FFF7ED", "#F0FDF4", "#EFF6FF"), edge = c("#6B7280", "#7C3AED", "#D97706", "#16A34A", "#2563EB"), title = c("ENVIRONMENT", "DATA LAYER", "MODELLING LAYER", "ADVANCED ANALYTICS", "DEPLOYMENT & GOVERNANCE"), tools = c( "R 4.3 · Quarto / RStudio · packages.R / renv · Git / GitHub", "tidyverse · dplyr · ggplot2 · sf · stats · naniar · digest", "tidymodels · xgboost · lightgbm · DALEX · survival · broom · quanteda · text2vec", "Causal Inference (dagitty / PS / DiD / ITS / IV / TMLE) · Spatial Epidemiology (LISA / BYM / GWR / Scan)", "plumber · shiny · MLflow · Docker · Quarto · GitHub Actions · Model Cards" ) ) p_stack <- ggplot(layers) + geom_rect( aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = face, colour = edge), linewidth = 1.1 ) + geom_text( aes(x = xmin + 0.35, y = ymax - Key Terms Quick Reference | Term | Module | Meaning | |------|--------|---------| | **AUC-ROC** | 04 | Area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve; model discrimination | | **Brier score** | 04 | Mean squared error of probability predictions; measures calibration | | **DCA** | 04 | Decision Curve Analysis; net benefit of a model at a given risk threshold | | **SHAP** | 04 | SHapley Additive exPlanations; feature contribution scores per patient | | **DAG** | 06 | Directed Acyclic Graph; encodes causal assumptions about variable relationships | | **IPTW** | 06 | Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting; creates a pseudo-randomised sample | | **TMLE** | 06 | Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation; doubly-robust causal effect estimator | | **DiD** | 06 | Difference-in-Differences; compares treated vs control groups before/after a policy | | **ITS** | 06 | Interrupted Time Series; evaluates policy effects using temporal trends | | **SMR** | 07 | Standardised Mortality Ratio; observed / expected deaths in a population | | **LISA** | 07 | Local Indicators of Spatial Association; identifies local spatial clusters | | **BYM** | 07 | Besag-York-Mollié model; Bayesian disease mapping with CAR/ICAR prior | | **GWR** | 07 | Geographically Weighted Regression; spatially varying coefficient model | | **2SFCA** | 07 | Two-Step Floating Catchment Area; healthcare access metric | | **E-value** | 06 | Minimum confounding effect size needed to explain away an observed association | | **HPSA** | 07 | Health Professional Shortage Area (federal US designation) | | **PHI** | 05 | Protected Health Information (HIPAA-regulated patient identifiers) | | **SaMD** | 08 | Software as a Medical Device (FDA classification for clinical AI) | | **Model Card** | 08 | Structured documentation of a model's intended use, performance, and limitations | ## 8.
